agent_dependency_layer.cross_substrate_note: Every node names its rac_analog: the SAME failure mechanism priced in dollars on the infrastructure substrate (rac dependency_catalog.json) appears here in structural units on the agent substrate. One portfolio, one mechanism, two substrates.

deferred_nodes.note: DECLARED DEFERRALS (same discipline as rac C30.6): agent-layer common-cause classes recognized but not yet modeled as first-class nodes — deferred, not denied.

anchors.name: CrowdStrike Falcon content update
anchors.summary: The defense plane itself became the outage — the class precedent for 'the control watching the estate is the single point of failure'; rac prices the infrastructure twin as security_agent_vendor.

anchors.name: Cloudflare WAF regex CPU exhaustion
anchors.summary: A safety-layer rule change took the protected estate down globally in minutes — the governance layer as common cause, not just common observer.

nodes.blast_basis: governs every traced action by construction (the detection plane)
nodes.blindness_effect: THE defining mode: the classifier still routes traffic but no longer catches. Detections drop to zero while violations continue — absorbed violations accumulate unlogged, and the dashboard reads GREEN precisely because the control watching the agents went dark. The divergence thesis rac prices on its skew-and-backpressure pattern, replayed on the agent substrate: level-metrics are what a silent classifier masks.
nodes.loss_effect: The evaluation pipeline is DOWN — visibly. A gap opens in the finding log and everyone knows the estate is running unwatched; painful but honest.
nodes.mitigation_note: Canary violations (synthetic known-bad traces injected continuously) are the only honest heartbeat for a detection plane — a classifier that stops flagging the canaries is dark, whatever its uptime says.
nodes.name: Safety / governance classifier plane (the detection layer itself)

anchors.label: CLASS_ANALOG
anchors.name: Meta control-plane loss
anchors.summary: The control plane that routes everything goes down and takes the tools that would fix it — no public agent-orchestrator incident of record at this archetype; this is the nearest control-plane precedent, declared as an analog.

anchors.label: CLASS_ANALOG
anchors.name: Reddit Pi-Day K8s control-plane outage

nodes.blast_basis: derived from lineage edges of node 'agent-orchestrator'
nodes.blindness_effect: Routing continues but trace emission breaks — actions still happen, UNGOVERNED. A lineage break at estate scale: every downstream evidence trail is severed while work continues, and multi-agent loops run uncounted.
nodes.loss_effect: Every workflow stalls — no delegation, no tool calls, no decisions. The estate's single structural hub: its loss IS the estate's loss.
nodes.mitigation_note: The one node whose blast radius the lineage graph itself proves: it transits every workflow. Isolation options are structural (per-domain orchestrators, static fallback routing), not control tweaks.
nodes.name: Agent orchestrator (routing & delegation plane)

anchors.name: Okta support-system breach
anchors.summary: Session tokens lifted from support artifacts — the issuer of trust as the breach vector; every relying integration inherited the compromise.

anchors.name: CircleCI secrets compromise
anchors.summary: 'Rotate everything' — one broker-level compromise invalidated every secret it had ever held; the blast radius is the credential graph, not the incident.

anchors.name: tj-actions/changed-files supply-chain compromise
anchors.summary: A compromised CI action exfiltrated repository secrets at scale — automation credentials as the soft target of the estate.

nodes.blast_basis: derived from traces with action_type in ['data_read', 'data_write', 'external_api_call']
nodes.blindness_effect: COMPROMISE rather than outage: agent credentials exfiltrated or the issuer breached — actions execute with stolen agent authority, indistinguishable from governed work until the trail is audited. The agent estate's account-takeover.
nodes.loss_effect: Agents cannot authenticate to the systems they read and write — every data-touching workflow stalls at first credential refresh.
nodes.mitigation_note: Short-lived per-workflow tokens bound to declared scopes turn a broker compromise from estate-wide to workflow-wide — the same containment-boundary move rac prices on the infrastructure side.
nodes.name: Credential broker (agent secrets & token issuance)

anchors.name: OpenAI major API outage
anchors.summary: API and ChatGPT down for hours (DDoS-attributed) — every dependent product's agent layer stalled at once; the pure form of this node's loss mode.

anchors.name: ChatGPT/API multi-hour degradation
anchors.summary: Elevated errors across the API during peak hours — dependent workflows degraded together, not independently.

nodes.blast_basis: derived from traces with action_type in ['model_inference']
nodes.blindness_effect: The provider degrades SILENTLY — a model swap, a quality regression, a routing change. Agents keep producing output that clears no bar: low-confidence decisions ship and PII discipline slips, with nothing down to alarm on.
nodes.loss_effect: Every agent that reasons stops reasoning — inference is the substrate the estate runs on, and a provider outage is a same-hour, all-workflows event.
nodes.mitigation_note: Multi-provider failover is the region-failover of the agent estate — and carries the same failover-failure risk class rac prices on cloud_region (the fallback model behaves differently under the same prompts).
nodes.name: Model provider (hosted LLM inference)

anchors.name: postmark-mcp — first malicious MCP package on a public registry
anchors.summary: A typosquatted MCP server BCC'd every email it relayed to an attacker domain — tool-supply-chain compromise executing with full agent authority.

anchors.name: CVE-2025-49596 · MCP Inspector RCE (CVSS 9.4)
anchors.summary: RCE in the standard MCP debugging tool — the tooling AROUND the agent supply chain is itself attack surface.

nodes.blast_basis: derived from traces with action_type in ['tool_execution', 'external_api_call']
nodes.blindness_effect: The registry is POISONED rather than down — a malicious or tampered tool description executes with the agent's authority: data exfiltrates through 'legitimate' tool calls, scope walks outward one plausible call at a time, copies accumulate where no policy looks.
nodes.loss_effect: Tool resolution fails — every workflow that executes a tool or calls an external API stalls at the call site.
nodes.mitigation_note: Hash-pinned tool manifests and registry attestation are the lockfile discipline of the agent layer; the ai-gov panel's hash-pin compliance metric reads on exactly this node.
nodes.name: Tool / MCP registry (agent supply chain)

agent_dependency_layer.one_thing: One agent-layer dependency — the Safety / governance classifier plane (the detection layer itself) — transits 16 of 16 workflows: the estate has a control plane, and this layer puts it on the register. Its blindness mode is the sharper edge: the classifier plane going dark unmasks every finding class at once while the dashboard reads green.
agent_dependency_layer.provenance_note: OPERATOR_CALIBRATED structure anchored to named public incidents. Where the class has no public incident of record at this archetype (a first-party agent orchestrator), anchors are labeled CLASS_ANALOG and borrow the nearest control-plane precedent — declared, not hidden.
agent_dependency_layer.units_note: STRUCTURAL LAYER, NOT A LOSS MODEL: atg's currency is workflows, traced actions and findings — there is deliberately NO frequency×severity dollar model here (the rac spoke prices the infrastructure analogs; production would attach fitted agent-incident history before pricing this layer). Blast radii are DERIVED at build time from the same traces and lineage the dashboard renders — the catalog declares WHAT each node underlies (lineage node or action types), never the counts.

anchors.name: ChatGPT — Redis bug exposed conversation titles and payment metadata
anchors.summary: Request-cancellation race in redis-py exposed chat titles and partial payment data for ~1.2% of ChatGPT Plus subscribers. Canonical 'shared cache + agent output' PII-leak class.

anchors.name: Samsung — semiconductor source code pasted into ChatGPT
anchors.summary: Three separate engineer-driven leaks of proprietary semiconductor source code and meeting transcripts to ChatGPT within 20 days. Samsung banned generative-AI tools company-wide on 2023-05-01.

anchors.name: Meta — Irish DPC €390M fine for Article 6 violation
anchors.summary: Irish Data Protection Commission fined Meta €210M (Facebook) + €180M (Instagram) for relying on 'contract' legal basis to process personal data for behavioural advertising without valid consent. Canonical 'consent assumed not captured' GDPR case.

anchors.name: Capital One — SSRF to AWS metadata service
anchors.summary: WAF misconfiguration allowed SSRF; attacker reached EC2 instance metadata service and exfiltrated ~106M records to external infrastructure. $80M OCC fine; consent order specifically cited absent egress controls.

anchors.name: Samsung — proprietary code to external LLM endpoint
anchors.summary: Engineer-initiated paste of proprietary semiconductor code to a third-party model service — the canonical agent-era external-flow violation (the destination is a model API, not a competitor).

anchors.name: CVE-2025-49596 — MCP Inspector RCE (CVSS 9.4)
anchors.summary: Unauthenticated MCP Inspector instances allowed arbitrary command execution — an agent-tooling 'open scope' failure exposed to network.

anchors.name: Tool-mutation / rug-pull pattern (Simon Willison)
anchors.summary: MCP tool definitions can mutate after install; a tool approved on Day 1 can be re-pointed by Day 7 with no re-approval. The scope a user authorized is not the scope the tool ends up exercising.

anchors.name: Moffatt v. Air Canada — airline liable for chatbot hallucination
anchors.summary: BC Civil Resolution Tribunal held Air Canada liable for chatbot-invented bereavement-refund policy ($812.02). Court rejected airline's 'separate legal entity' defence — companies own their agents' decisions. The first agent-confidence ruling that bit a deployer.

anchors.name: Zillow Offers — model drift in production
anchors.summary: iBuying model overpaid for inventory in a volatile market; Zillow wound down Offers with a $304M write-down and ~25% workforce reduction. Confidence intervals existed; they did not surface to a decision veto in time.

anchors.name: Atlassian Cloud — 14-day partial outage
anchors.summary: Maintenance script deleted ~775 customer sites; recovery took up to 14 days for some tenants because per-tenant restore tooling and lineage between operational and backup state did not exist.

anchors.name: Amazon — CNPD €746M fine (Luxembourg)
anchors.summary: Largest GDPR fine to date at issuance; Luxembourg DPA found Amazon's personal-data processing did not comply with GDPR rules, including retention and lawful-basis concerns.

anchors.name: MCPTox benchmark — agent vulnerability to tool-output prompt injection
anchors.summary: Benchmark tested 20 LLM agents against 45 real MCP servers; most agents were vulnerable to prompt-injection-driven action loops via tool descriptions and outputs. Loops are the failure mode; injection is the trigger.

patterns_meta.source_note: Authoritative RE taxonomy + framework citations + incident anchors from data/action_schema.json. Anchors are keyed to the RE class and render only in the ATTEST/PATTERN precedent register — never inside a finding's impact band (port spec §14.A.3 / §15.C).
